quotes.text: Migrate your mobile app to an integration that can handle bank requests for card authentication.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Instead, the PaymentIntent status changes to `requires_action`.
If successful, the PaymentIntent will have a status of `requires_confirmation` and you need to confirm the PaymentIntent again on your server to finish the payment.
The payment attempt fails and transitions back to `requires_payment_method` if it isn’t confirmed again within one hour.
In live mode the bank controls the UI of what’s displayed inside the modal.
Requires authentication, which in this integration will fail with a decline code of `authentication_not_handled`.

findings: New raw lines 5–15 retain the mobile migration purpose and link the same iOS, Android and React Native variants that were inline on April 23, 2026 (old raw lines 1–10, 194–196 and 392–394). The November variant bodies were not read. Diff line 564 concatenates the deleted test row and iOS link. The two pinned raws establish each side independently.

The April guide assumes an existing basic mobile card integration and existing intent-create endpoint. Initial request provides a PaymentMethod ID. Server creates and confirms a card PaymentIntent with `confirmation_method: 'manual'` and `use_stripe_sdk: true`, dropping `error_on_requires_action`. The server sends the same Intent's client secret if customer action is needed. After successful action, the client sends its PaymentIntent ID for explicit server reconfirmation (old raw lines 12–43, 72–96, 110–126 and 139–182).

Source lines 47–54 skip the post-action `requires_confirmation` state and read as a fixed two-round-trip flow with an open-ended loop. The April sample's simple success path may succeed on the first server attempt. When action is required, the mobile handler completing it leads to `requires_confirmation` and the server explicitly confirms the same PaymentIntent again. Fulfillment is the server's `succeeded` branch, separate from client handler success, cancel, timeout, or failure (old raw lines 72-96, 110-126, 139-182, 303-330 and 473-553). The separately read November Confirm API distinguishes automatic confirmation and limits manual reconfirmations, with `canceled` after the variable limit (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07.md:7-17`); the API also distinguishes manual capture and `requires_capture` from manual confirmation. Qualify the in-app concept's line 115 and Stripe index line 129 to retain the April manual path and its one-hour behavior without universalizing them.

The April upgrade guide's sandbox text describes a fake modal that can simulate authentication success and failure, but its repeated test-card row says the authentication-required card fails in this integration with `authentication_not_handled` (old raw lines 184-192, 382-390 and 555-563). The separate April basic mobile guide gives that same row for its decline-instead-of-authentication flow and shows `error.code: authentication_required` with `decline_code: authentication_not_handled` (related raw `raw/stripe-inapp-without-card-auth-2025.md:285-325`). The November Testing page classifies the same test card as requiring on-session authentication and describes off-session setup separately (`raw/stripe-testing-2026-11-07.md:805-818`). Keep the dated mismatch visible in the upgrade and basic mobile guide routes. Preserve `requires_action_not_handled` as the April upgrade introduction's diagnostic wording, not a guaranteed API matcher or a synonym for the test decline code (old raw lines 12-17; `raw/stripe-decline-codes-2026.md:8-16,20-21`). The link-only November upgrade capture does not resolve the mismatch or prove an actual test result.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the explicitly dated April 23, 2026 manual-confirm path and its one-hour reconfirmation warning. Expiry of the guide's window is described as an attempt failure returning to `requires_payment_method` (old raw lines 139–142, 337–340 and 510–513). The separate November Confirm API gives general lifecycle and variable confirmation limit, not a renewal of that guide-specific duration.

The iOS Objective-C example uses `STPPaymentHandler` and `STPAuthenticationContext`. The Android Java example uses `handleNextActionForPayment`, `onActivityResult` and `onPaymentResult`, and React Native uses `handleCardAction` via `useStripe` in the `requires_action` branch. Preserve those API names as April example evidence and avoid making them current SDK minimums or universal methods. Treat `requires_confirmation` as an intermediate state and client handler success as successful handling of the action, distinct from server `succeeded` (old raw lines 91–137, 277–335 and 473–508).

Retain the dated sandbox versus live UI distinction: sandbox simulates both authentication outcomes with a fake page, and the issuer controls live modal content. Keep the contradictory test row visible as dated wording and cite the separate authority when interpreting it (old raw lines 184–192, 382–390 and 555–563).

The separate November testing page identifies the card's authentication requirements, but the November upgrade index contains no revised test or release-specific platform details.

Restore the omitted intermediate state, first-attempt success possibility, and distinction between client action success and payment completion. A maintainer asking which state or result authorizes fulfillment could otherwise read the SDK success callback and two-round sequence as payment success after the modal.

The source ends its implementation guidance without the contradictory test row, despite summarizing the `requires_action_not_handled` observation. A maintainer looking up how to interpret a failure in the authentication-required sandbox case could miss the mismatch in a long platform-packed raw.

source_assessments.reason: The November raw is a navigation reference. The baseline needs the `requires_confirmation` and server success boundaries, a qualification on repeat confirmation, and a dated reciprocal warning about test and error-code wording.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions states the goal of migrating a basic mobile card integration to handle issuer authentication and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The April 23, 2026 guide assumes the prior no-action card integration and a merchant server endpoint. A client-supplied PaymentMethod ID starts the payment attempt. The server removes `error_on_requires_action` and creates and confirms the card PaymentIntent with `confirmation_method: 'manual'` and `use_stripe_sdk: true` (old raw lines 12-41). The server's `succeeded` branch can trigger fulfillment immediately. On `requires_action`, the server returns the PaymentIntent client secret so the applicable mobile SDK can prompt authentication. Successful action leaves the PaymentIntent in `requires_confirmation`. The client sends that same PaymentIntent's ID for server reconfirmation and fulfillment follows a final `succeeded` result (old raw lines 72-96, old raw lines 110-126 and old raw lines 139-182). The April guide says the attempt returns to `requires_payment_method` when reconfirmation misses its one-hour window. source-stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions.md preserves the flags and ID handoff but skips the intermediate state and the distinction between client action success and payment success.
answers.Q2: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions changes the presentation to three links for the same platform variants (new raw lines 9-15). source-stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions.md should retain the April 23, 2026 manual path, its one-hour warning, and its dated iOS Objective-C, Android Java and React Native handler examples (old raw lines 91-142, old raw lines 277-340 and old raw lines 473-513). An SDK action callback signals action handling. Server-confirmed `succeeded` is the fulfillment boundary in the guide. The November Confirm API separately distinguishes automatic mode, manual capture, and a variable limit on repeated manual confirmation (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07.md:7-17`). In April, the sandbox modal can simulate authentication success or failure and the live issuer controls modal content. The repeated row still says the authentication-required test card fails with `authentication_not_handled` (old raw lines 184-192 and old raw lines 555-563). The April no-action predecessor shows that value as a decline code with API error `authentication_required`, while the April upgrade intro uses `requires_action_not_handled` (old raw lines 12-17; `raw/stripe-inapp-without-card-auth-2025.md:290-325`). The November testing page describes the same test card's on-session authentication requirement (`raw/stripe-testing-2026-11-07.md:805-818`). Preserve the diagnostic and test-table mismatch on both guide routes with date and field scope. The November index supplies no implementation update, SDK-version refresh, or actual payment result.
